claim_ceiling: Scoped comparison on one frozen ten-body Newtonian workload; not a universal engine ranking, full DE441 reconstruction, or Planet-X claim.

workload.units: AU, day, GM as AU^3/day^2, G=1
workload.comparison_coordinates: heliocentric differences formed independently at every output

lanes.y6_cached: JX seven-map sixth-order Yoshida with boundary-force reuse
lanes.bm6: experimental Blanes-Moan optimized sixth-order S10/BM6 binary64 lane
lanes.referee: independent SciPy DOP853 force implementation, loose/tight pair

required_metrics: max and RMS heliocentric position error against DOP853
max and RMS heliocentric velocity error against DOP853
maximum and final relative energy error
reference_gate: DOP853 loose-vs-tight RMS position and velocity disagreement must each be <=1% of the best competing error.
win_rule: A JX lane wins only when all four all-body trajectory metrics are smaller than REBOUND and its energy and angular-momentum gates do not worsen. Equal-force-budget is primary; equal-timestep must not contradict it.
preservation: Do not modify existing KDK/Yoshida baselines, DE441 inputs, or historical results. Add only isolated benchmark code and generated artifacts.
